pathway.title: Crane NXT, Co. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is the central weakness because debt has grown far faster than reported earnings. Balance-sheet debt rose USD 737.6 million between 2023-12-31 and 2026-09-30, while last-twelve-months net sales are 33.32% above FY2023 and reported EBITDA only 2.47% above it, so the EBITDA margin fell from 26.19% to 20.13%. Net debt is 3.03x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.56x at year-end 2025, which is 3.57x once the Antares Vision second phase of 2026-03-31 is added to year-end net debt and 2.65x with the USD 31.1 million of nine-month dividends added alone; debt carries the acquisitions in full while earnings carry Antares Vision only from 2026-03-31. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation D5; calculation D3; calculation D4; calculation D1; calculation D2; calculation D15

Cash generation is the strongest support and keeps interest servicing comfortable. Free cash flow was USD 235.5 million over the last twelve months, 63.07% of reported EBITDA, EBITDA covered cash interest 5.62x, and liquidity of USD 821.2 million (cash plus undrawn revolver, before any letter of credit usage) is 3.55x short-term borrowings. Dividends took 22.29% of nine-month free cash flow and there were no buybacks, so distributions do not compete with debt reduction. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation D7; calculation D10; calculation D8; calculation D9; calculation D15

Earnings growth rests on one lumpy engine, security and authentication. Its operating profit rose 67.7% to USD 100.1 million in the first nine months on higher currency volumes, lifting its margin to 15.10% from 10.87%, yet one unnamed customer supplied 12.72% of FY2025 net sales, 26.01% of this segment's, and the full-year outlook implies fourth-quarter sales of this segment 9.47% below a year earlier, so the gain looks driven by award timing rather than a steady trend. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation D12; calculation D25; calculation D16

The payments and inspection segment is shrinking organically and is the weakest operating area. Detection and traceability organic sales fell 4.6% over nine months and 5.3% in Q3 on lower hardware and vending volumes, its operating margin dropped to 15.54% from 25.28% partly on Antares Vision amortisation, and acquisitions supplied 76.24% of the group's nine-month sales increase. On the issuer's adjusted basis the segment margin fell only 2.5 percentage points to 27.0%, so part of the decline is acquisition accounting and part is genuine volume weakness. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation D12; calculation D14; calculation D33; calculation D34

Refinancing is not a near-term pressure, but rate and covenant exposure are rising. No bank facility matures before 2030-12-15, when the revolver and Term Loan A, 22.50% of carrying debt, fall due; the Term Loan B was repriced and increased to EUR 480.0 million on 2026-07-02, at a margin of 2.0% to 2.25% over the euro interbank rate against a credit spread of 2.75% stated at year-end 2025; the 2036 and 2048 notes carry no material covenants; and the agencies rated the company BB+ and Ba1 with stable outlooks at 2025-12-31, before the Antares Vision second phase. Against that, 60.94% of debt now floats against 53% at year-end 2025, and, reading completion of the Antares Vision purchase as 2026-03-31, the permitted maximum total net leverage ratio steps down from 5.00x at 2026-09-30 to 4.25x from Q2 2027, while no ratio, definition or compliance statement is supplied, so headroom is not calculable. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D20; calculation D6; calculation D38; calculation D39; calculation D42

Acquisition accounting adds a non-cash risk that would still weigh on confidence. Goodwill and intangible assets are 60.21% of total assets, and the annual report's sensitivity test at year-end 2025 left the recently acquired Authentication reporting unit, 27.9% of goodwill then, with a fair value cushion of less than 10%, so a shortfall in acquired earnings would show as impairment as well as weaker cash flow. Minority shares in the Antares Vision vehicle and pension liabilities add USD 84.5 million, 0.23x reported EBITDA, outside reported debt; the Class B shares carry put and call features once converted, but their price, timing and settlement form are not disclosed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation D24; calculation D19

Financial policy is measured on distributions but acquisitive, and acquisitions are the main behavioural risk. Consideration of USD 1,076.4 million for three purchases since May 2024 was funded mainly with revolver and term loan debt, the dividend is USD 0.18 per share a quarter, no open-market repurchases were made in 2026, and no sponsor or controlling holder is named, although the proxy statement that would show board independence was not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 34; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D28; calculation D15; calculation D40

runs.text: The strongest credit support is cash generation: free cash flow of USD 235.5 million over twelve months and EBITDA cover of cash interest of 5.62x mean debt service does not depend on refinancing, and liquidity of USD 821.2 million covers short-term borrowings 3.55x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D7; calculation D10; calculation D8; calculation D9

A second support is the shape of the debt: no bank facility falls due before 2030-12-15 and the 2036 and 2048 notes carry no material covenants or cross default provisions, so a weak year does not force a near-term refinancing. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D20

A third support is visibility: an order book of USD 715.5 million with 94% due within two years, and security and authentication organic sales up 11.6% over nine months, which give the company time to integrate Antares Vision. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation D23; calculation D33

The main weakness is leverage that has outrun earnings: debt rose USD 737.6 million since 2023-12-31 while reported EBITDA rose 2.47%, so net debt over reported EBITDA is 3.03x and any earnings miss lifts it directly. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D5; calculation D4; calculation D1

A second weakness is the payments and inspection segment, where organic sales fell 4.6% over nine months and operating margin fell to 15.54% from 25.28%, so the acquired growth is masking a shrinking base. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation D12; calculation D33

A third weakness is concentration and timing: one unnamed customer is 12.72% of sales and banknote awards vary in timing and size, so a delayed award reaches cash flow and leverage within a quarter. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation D25

A fourth weakness is exposure that is growing: 60.94% of debt floats, the permitted covenant maximum steps down to 4.25x by Q2 2027 with no compliance figure supplied, and goodwill and intangibles are 60.21% of assets. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation D6; calculation D39; calculation D24

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Antares Vision purchase is the central transaction. Crane NXT bought a 32.3% interest on 2025-12-16 for EUR 117.3 million and completed a tender offer and squeeze-out on 2026-03-31 for EUR 244.2 million, a total consideration of USD 416.9 million including the remeasured earlier interest. It was funded with the new EUR Term Loan B, and Antares Vision personnel reinvested through ordinary and Class B shares of the acquisition vehicle, so part of the acquired equity sits outside the parent. The purchase price allocation is still preliminary, with goodwill of USD 263.1 million and borrowings assumed of USD 132.3 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation K22

The two earlier purchases were also debt-funded. OpSec Security, bought on 2024-05-03 for a USD 270 million base price, drew USD 210.0 million on the revolver. De La Rue Authentication, bought on 2025-05-01 for a GBP 300 million base price (net cash paid USD 391.1 million), was funded with the delayed-draw Term Loan A and brought a consolidated Ghana tax stamp joint venture in which the company owns 49% but controls the board. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83

New debt came only through bank facility amendments. The Fifth Amendment on 2025-12-15 added a EUR 430 million Term Loan B to 2032-12-15, lifted the revolver to USD 800.0 million and extended the revolver and Term Loan A to 2030-12-15. The Sixth Amendment on 2026-07-02 repriced Term Loan B and raised it to EUR 480.0 million at a margin of 2.0% to 2.25%, with the extra proceeds and cash on hand used to repay part of Term Loan A. A 364-day USD 602 million bridge and a USD 831 million backstop were committed in September 2025 and terminated once term debt was placed. No new notes were issued; the 2036 and 2048 notes are the only bonds outstanding. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Crane NXT, Co. (issuer cxt-25445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: FY2023 to FY2025 and nine-month 2026 statements, debt at carrying value, leverage and cover on reported EBITDA, with the issuer's adjusted measures beside them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage on reported earnings rose after the Antares Vision purchase: net debt was 3.03x LTM EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.56x at year-end 2025, so creditors carry more debt against earnings that include the acquired business only from March 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C4; calculation C10; calculation C38

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA covered cash interest 5.62x over the last twelve months against 6.35x for FY2025. The company's own net leverage of 2.5x is lower because it adds pre-acquisition earnings of the acquired business and issuer add-backs; the two bases cannot be reconciled from the documents supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C39; calculation C31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage rose at each year-end and again at the latest quarter because debt grew faster than earnings. Net debt over reported EBITDA moved from 1.15x at FY2023 to 1.64x, 2.56x and 3.03x at FY2024, FY2025 and 2026-09-30, while EBITDA stayed between USD 353.3 million and USD 373.4 million. The 2025 De La Rue Authentication purchase and the 2026 Antares Vision purchase were funded mainly with term loans, so debt carries both in full while earnings carry the first from May 2025 and the second from March 2026 only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover shows the same shift. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 8.08x in FY2023 and 8.06x in FY2024, then 6.35x in FY2025 and 5.62x over the last twelve months, because cash interest paid rose from USD 44.1 million in FY2024 to USD 66.4 million as the debt stack grew. Cover remains above 5x, so interest servicing is not the constraint these figures show; whether a covenant ceiling is a constraint cannot be established because no covenant ratio is reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C39; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a rising-leverage reading is the company's own series: 2.9x, 2.7x and 2.5x at the three 2026 quarter-ends, with company net debt falling by USD 150.0 million to USD 1,161.5 million while its TTM Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 448.9 million to USD 460.3 million. That series counts Antares Vision earnings from before it was owned and issuer add-backs; it would prevail if the pre-acquisition amounts were supplied and confirmed on a consistent definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow was USD 235.5 million over the last twelve months, after operating cash flow of USD 290.3 million and capital expenditure of USD 54.8 million, or 0.63 of reported EBITDA against 0.56 in FY2025. Acquisition payments of USD 225.4 million net of cash acquired and dividends of USD 31.1 million in the nine months of 2026 were paid from that cash flow and from term loan and revolver borrowings, so net debt rose even as free cash flow stayed positive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of USD 251.1 million plus an undrawn revolver of USD 570.1 million, USD 821.2 million in total, against USD 231.1 million of borrowings classified as short-term. Letters of credit usage of the revolver is not stated, so availability may be lower. The only maturity ladder is at year-end 2025: USD 9.1 million falls due in 2026 and USD 27.2 million in 2027 to 2028, with USD 326.3 million in 2029 to 2030. It appears to omit the revolver and predates the 2026 refinancing steps, so the maturity wall after 2026 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C23; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contract liabilities, interest-free customer funding that is not debt, were USD 158.4 million at 2026-09-30, USD 71.1 million above 2025-12-31 on the 2026 presentation, of which USD 46.9 million came with Antares Vision. They fund operations at no interest cost; a fall without matching deliveries would draw on cash, and the filings give no customer deposit terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt appears on three bases in the documents: carrying value on the balance sheet, principal before deferred financing costs in the company's net leverage table (USD 30.1 million higher at 2026-09-30), and the contractual obligations table, which sits USD 95.3 million below carrying value at 2025-12-31 and appears to leave out the revolver. This module uses carrying value and shows the others beside it. Reported EBITDA here is operating profit plus depreciation and amortization; the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA is USD 52.5 million higher for the nine months of 2026 because it adds back transaction, acquisition and restructuring items and starts from net income, so it also holds non-operating income.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Crane NXT, Co. (issuer cxt-25445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: business and operating model, ownership, transactions, history and governance and financial-policy behaviour, from the supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Crane NXT is a specialised, acquisition-led technology group whose creditors depend on contract-driven security revenue and a payments business with shrinking organic sales, while the governance evidence supplied is too thin to confirm or rule out a controlling holder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt-funded purchases of USD 1,076.4 million since May 2024 lifted goodwill and intangibles to 60.21% of assets, and one unnamed customer supplied 12.72% of FY2025 sales. Dividends are 19.67% of free cash flow and there are no buybacks, so sponsor and governance risk is rated Medium on incomplete evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K5; calculation K3; calculation K1; calculation K7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is specialised and technology-led, which supports retention but concentrates demand. Crane NXT sells proprietary security features, authentication and payment or inspection equipment to central banks, governments, brands and vending, retail and gaming operators, and describes itself as a principal competitor in most of its markets. One unnamed security customer supplied 12.72% of FY2025 net sales and banknote awards, notably from the U.S. government, vary in timing and size, so a delayed award would cut debt service capacity directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation K1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported growth is acquisition-led while the payments and inspection segment is shrinking organically. In Q3 2026 the detection and traceability segment's organic sales fell 5.3% while acquisitions added 23.1%, and the security segment's organic sales rose 7.2%. Management lowered its full-year sales growth outlook to about 14% from a range of 15% to 17%, which is an untested management statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition appetite is the main behavioural signal and it adds debt faster than earnings. Consideration of USD 1,076.4 million across OpSec, De La Rue Authentication and Antares Vision was funded with revolver and term loan borrowings; balance-sheet debt rose by USD 737.6 million between 2023-12-31 and 2026-09-30 and goodwill and intangibles reached 60.21% of total assets, so an integration miss would appear as impairment as well as lower cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation K5; calculation K8; calculation K3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Distributions are modest and creditor-neutral on the evidence read. Dividends of USD 39.0 million were 19.67% of FY2025 free cash flow, the quarterly dividend rose by 5.88% to USD 0.18 per share, no open-market repurchases were made in any quarter of 2026, and no sponsor, management fee or related-party leakage appears in the filings read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation K7; calculation K9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership and board detail cannot be established, so the risk level rests on behaviour rather than structure. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, but board composition, independence, compensation and beneficial ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Management reinvestment in the Antares Vision acquisition vehicle adds minority claims of USD 20.6 million in ordinary shares and USD 36.1 million in Class B shares at fair value, with put and call terms not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting is adequate for monitoring but silent on covenants. Quarterly reports and releases are timely and audit opinions are unqualified, but revenue recognised over time on U.S. government contracts is a critical audit matter, management excluded De La Rue Authentication from its FY2025 internal-control assessment, and no covenant ratio or compliance statement is published.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium risk view is the absence of any extraction: no sponsor, no fee stream, no buybacks, dividends at 19.67% of free cash flow, unqualified audits and a backlog of USD 715.5 million of which 94% is due within two years. Management also says it is on track for a year-end deleveraging target and reports falling company net leverage. That view would win if the proxy statement showed dispersed ownership and independent oversight, and if the target proved to be set at a conservative level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation K7; calculation K23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to High if the proxy statement showed a controlling holder with a record of debt-funded distributions, if the credit agreement allowed wide restricted payments, or if a further debt-funded acquisition were announced before leverage fell. It would move to Low if the acquired Antares Vision business showed organic growth and the put and call terms were small and fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so the Medium rating changes to Low if it shows dispersed beneficial ownership and independent oversight, and to High if it shows a controlling holder with a distribution record.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied, so capital allocation is judged by what was done and not by what is permitted; broad restricted payment or acquisition capacity would raise the risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Results of Antares Vision before 2026-03-31 were not supplied, so the enlarged detection and traceability segment shows acquisition-driven growth without a like-for-like trend; a stable acquired base would soften the organic-decline finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The significant customer is unnamed and no contract term is disclosed, so the concentration finding cannot be sized beyond its FY2025 share of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Put and call terms for management reinvestment are not disclosed, so the cash-call risk below the parent is directional only and could be larger or smaller.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Antares Vision purchase is the central transaction. Crane NXT bought a 32.3% interest on 2025-12-16 for EUR 117.3 million and completed a tender offer and squeeze-out on 2026-03-31 for EUR 244.2 million, a total consideration of USD 416.9 million including the remeasured earlier interest. It was funded with the new EUR Term Loan B, and Antares Vision personnel reinvested through ordinary and Class B shares of the acquisition vehicle, so part of the acquired equity sits outside the parent. The purchase price allocation is still preliminary, with goodwill of USD 263.1 million and borrowings assumed of USD 132.3 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation K22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The two earlier purchases were also debt-funded. OpSec Security, bought on 2024-05-03 for a USD 270 million base price, drew USD 210.0 million on the revolver. De La Rue Authentication, bought on 2025-05-01 for a GBP 300 million base price (net cash paid USD 391.1 million), was funded with the delayed-draw Term Loan A and brought a consolidated Ghana tax stamp joint venture in which the company owns 49% but controls the board.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt came only through bank facility amendments. The Fifth Amendment on 2025-12-15 added a EUR 430 million Term Loan B to 2032-12-15, lifted the revolver to USD 800.0 million and extended the revolver and Term Loan A to 2030-12-15. The Sixth Amendment on 2026-07-02 repriced Term Loan B and raised it to EUR 480.0 million at a margin of 2.0% to 2.25%, with the extra proceeds and cash on hand used to repay part of Term Loan A. A 364-day USD 602 million bridge and a USD 831 million backstop were committed in September 2025 and terminated once term debt was placed. No new notes were issued; the 2036 and 2048 notes are the only bonds outstanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Crane NXT presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is a run of debt-funded acquisitions totalling USD 1,076.4 million since May 2024, which matters because debt rises before the acquired earnings are in the base and goodwill grows, and it implies higher refinancing and impairment risk if integration disappoints. Countervailing evidence is modest dividends, no buybacks and no sponsor or fee leakage. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the pre-acquisition results of Antares Vision. Governance work completed with limitations. Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Crane NXT, Co. (issuer cxt-25445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: business and operating model, cash flow durability, leverage tolerance, liquidity, refinancing capacity, financial policy, downside path and monitoring triggers, from the supplied filings and releases and the three earlier modules' results. Covenant headroom, structural priority and recovery are outside this module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Crane NXT is a cash-generative specialist whose debt-funded acquisitions have lifted leverage faster than earnings, so creditors depend on integration and banknote award timing to restore deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D1; calculation D4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt is 3.03x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.56x at year-end 2025, or 3.57x once the Antares Vision second phase of 2026-03-31 is added to year-end net debt (2.65x with nine months of dividends added instead). Free cash flow of USD 235.5 million over twelve months and liquidity of USD 821.2 million are the main support. The weakest area is payments and inspection, with organic sales down 4.6% over nine months, and covenant headroom cannot be calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the central weakness because debt has grown far faster than reported earnings. Balance-sheet debt rose USD 737.6 million between 2023-12-31 and 2026-09-30, while last-twelve-months net sales are 33.32% above FY2023 and reported EBITDA only 2.47% above it, so the EBITDA margin fell from 26.19% to 20.13%. Net debt is 3.03x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.56x at year-end 2025, which is 3.57x once the Antares Vision second phase of 2026-03-31 is added to year-end net debt and 2.65x with the USD 31.1 million of nine-month dividends added alone; debt carries the acquisitions in full while earnings carry Antares Vision only from 2026-03-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the strongest support and keeps interest servicing comfortable. Free cash flow was USD 235.5 million over the last twelve months, 63.07% of reported EBITDA, EBITDA covered cash interest 5.62x, and liquidity of USD 821.2 million (cash plus undrawn revolver, before any letter of credit usage) is 3.55x short-term borrowings. Dividends took 22.29% of nine-month free cash flow and there were no buybacks, so distributions do not compete with debt reduction.

fields.value: Earnings growth rests on one lumpy engine, security and authentication. Its operating profit rose 67.7% to USD 100.1 million in the first nine months on higher currency volumes, lifting its margin to 15.10% from 10.87%, yet one unnamed customer supplied 12.72% of FY2025 net sales, 26.01% of this segment's, and the full-year outlook implies fourth-quarter sales of this segment 9.47% below a year earlier, so the gain looks driven by award timing rather than a steady trend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The payments and inspection segment is shrinking organically and is the weakest operating area. Detection and traceability organic sales fell 4.6% over nine months and 5.3% in Q3 on lower hardware and vending volumes, its operating margin dropped to 15.54% from 25.28% partly on Antares Vision amortisation, and acquisitions supplied 76.24% of the group's nine-month sales increase. On the issuer's adjusted basis the segment margin fell only 2.5 percentage points to 27.0%, so part of the decline is acquisition accounting and part is genuine volume weakness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing is not a near-term pressure, but rate and covenant exposure are rising. No bank facility matures before 2030-12-15, when the revolver and Term Loan A, 22.50% of carrying debt, fall due; the Term Loan B was repriced and increased to EUR 480.0 million on 2026-07-02, at a margin of 2.0% to 2.25% over the euro interbank rate against a credit spread of 2.75% stated at year-end 2025; the 2036 and 2048 notes carry no material covenants; and the agencies rated the company BB+ and Ba1 with stable outlooks at 2025-12-31, before the Antares Vision second phase. Against that, 60.94% of debt now floats against 53% at year-end 2025, and, reading completion of the Antares Vision purchase as 2026-03-31, the permitted maximum total net leverage ratio steps down from 5.00x at 2026-09-30 to 4.25x from Q2 2027, while no ratio, definition or compliance statement is supplied, so headroom is not calculable.

fields.value: Acquisition accounting adds a non-cash risk that would still weigh on confidence. Goodwill and intangible assets are 60.21% of total assets, and the annual report's sensitivity test at year-end 2025 left the recently acquired Authentication reporting unit, 27.9% of goodwill then, with a fair value cushion of less than 10%, so a shortfall in acquired earnings would show as impairment as well as weaker cash flow. Minority shares in the Antares Vision vehicle and pension liabilities add USD 84.5 million, 0.23x reported EBITDA, outside reported debt; the Class B shares carry put and call features once converted, but their price, timing and settlement form are not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is measured on distributions but acquisitive, and acquisitions are the main behavioural risk. Consideration of USD 1,076.4 million for three purchases since May 2024 was funded mainly with revolver and term loan debt, the dividend is USD 0.18 per share a quarter, no open-market repurchases were made in 2026, and no sponsor or controlling holder is named, although the proxy statement that would show board independence was not supplied.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the company's own deleveraging record. Company net leverage was 2.9x, 2.7x and 2.5x at the three 2026 quarter-ends, company net debt fell USD 150.0 million from 2026-03-31, adjusted free cash flow conversion was 131.8% in Q3 and the order book of USD 715.5 million is 38.57% of last-twelve-months sales. The issuer's adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.0% over nine months against 23.9%, so underlying margin erosion is small. This view would win if Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31 and the fourth-quarter 2025 release confirmed the 2.5x on a consistent definition, closing the 0.51x gap to the house ratio, and if a compliance certificate showed wide headroom to the 4.75x maximum due at 2026-12-31 on the same reading of the completion date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Crane NXT sells proprietary security features, authentication, payment automation and inspection equipment to central banks, governments, brands and vending, retail and gaming operators, and describes itself as a principal competitor in most of its markets. Since 2026 it reports security and authentication with 48.11% of nine-month net sales and detection and traceability with 51.89%, the latter holding the former payments business and Antares Vision from 2026-03-31. The model supports cash-flow visibility through an order book of USD 715.5 million with 94% due within two years, but it concentrates demand in a few government and institutional buyers and exposes results to banknote award timing, so debt service capacity is sound while revenue is lumpy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Crane NXT is a New York Stock Exchange company formed by the separation of 2023-04-03, when the former Crane Holdings was split into two listed companies and Crane NXT kept the payment and merchandising technologies business, with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the filings read, so extraction risk is not evidenced but cannot be ruled out because board and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Structural claims matter more than shareholder behaviour here: the credit facilities are secured under a collateral agreement whose guarantor list is not supplied, the 2036 notes are described as secured senior obligations while the 2048 notes are senior notes, and their rank against the facilities is not stated, so the priority of any creditor group is not established. Antares Vision personnel hold USD 56.7 million of minority shares in the acquisition vehicle; the Class B shares carry put and call features once converted, but price, timing and settlement form are not disclosed, so a cash call below the parent is possible.

fields.value: Revenue is only partly predictable: it mixes lumpy government awards, cyclical equipment sales and growing services. Nine-month organic growth of 2.9% came from the currency business, with security and authentication organic sales up 11.6% and detection and traceability down 4.6%, where favourable pricing net of inflation was more than offset by lower hardware and vending volumes. Pricing power therefore exists but does not protect volume, so durability depends on award timing in one segment and equipment demand in the other; the order book gives about two years of visibility, one unnamed customer is 12.72% of sales, and the annual report names global trends in the use of cash and banknote durability as demand risks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are not stable, and productivity, volume and pricing have offset only part of acquisition amortisation and mix. Gross margin fell to 40.81% from 42.52% and operating margin to 11.38% from 14.16% over nine months: acquisition amortisation and unfavourable mix cost USD 68.1 million of operating profit, against offsets of USD 34.2 million from productivity and cost actions and USD 31.7 million from higher volumes and pricing net of inflation. The security segment's margin was 12.02% in FY2025 against 23.03% in FY2023, when higher material and manufacturing costs net of pricing cost USD 31.2 million and integration restructuring USD 12.1 million, which shows how input costs and acquired businesses can move profitability. Tariffs are expected to be largely offset by pricing and productivity and are not currently material, but some critical materials come from single or sole-source suppliers and the split of fixed and variable cost is not disclosed, so downside cost flexibility cannot be sized.

fields.value: Reported EBITDA converts into durable free cash flow today, but the conversion is exposed to a capital expenditure step-up and working capital swings. Capital expenditure is 2.95% of last-twelve-months sales, and the 2026 outlook of USD 75 million to USD 80 million implies USD 30.0 million to USD 35.0 million in Q4, about twice the nine-month quarterly average of USD 15.0 million. Customer prepayments recorded as contract liabilities reached USD 158.4 million, up USD 71.1 million of which USD 46.9 million came with Antares Vision, so USD 24.2 million is organic funding that would reverse if deliveries outran new orders, and the company's adjusted free cash flow conversion of -54.5% in Q1 against 131.8% in Q3 shows how uneven cash timing is within a year; the split between maintenance and growth capital expenditure is not disclosed, so flexibility over the maturity wall cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is real, since the company calls its markets highly competitive and says it is a principal competitor in most of them, but it cites technological differentiation in anti-counterfeiting materials and authentication software, which supports pricing but not volume in a weak cycle. Buyer power is the larger force: central banks and governments buy through awards that vary in timing and size and one customer is 12.72% of sales, so a lost or delayed award reaches debt service capacity directly. Supplier power is moderate, with single or sole-source suppliers for some critical materials that could interrupt production, and substitution is the structural risk to banknote demand, since the annual report names global trends in the use of cash and increased banknote durability. New entrants are not discussed in the filings read, so that force is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trade policy, currency and interest rates are the external factors that move credit quality. Tariffs are expected to be largely offset by pricing and productivity and are not currently material to results, but retaliatory measures could cut demand. Half of FY2025 sales were outside the United States and a 10% currency move would change net earnings by USD 7.4 million, which designating the Term Loan B and part of the revolver as net investment hedges partly offsets in equity; and 60.94% of debt floats against 53% at year-end 2025, when the issuer put a 1% rise in rates at USD 6.2 million of interest expense, so the exposure is now larger. Government budgets and central bank procurement drive security demand, while the annual report names advances in payment processing technologies and global trends in the use of cash as risks to demand for payment and banknote products.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is adequate today and weakening in trend. The main supports are cash generation, liquidity and the absence of bank maturities before 2030; the constraints are net debt of 3.03x reported EBITDA, a reported EBITDA margin that fell 6.06 percentage points between FY2023 and the last twelve months, and floating-rate debt at 60.94% of the total. Since FY2023 debt has risen USD 737.6 million while reported EBITDA rose 2.47%, and Antares Vision has still to show its earnings in full. Operating lease payments of USD 102.6 million and purchase obligations of USD 44.8 million at year-end 2025 sit outside reported debt, no factoring, supplier finance or securitisation is disclosed, and the Q2 report showed an interest rate swap inherited with Antares Vision of USD 36.2 million notional that the Q3 report no longer shows. The datapoints that would sharpen the view are the covenant definition and compliance, Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31, a maturity schedule, letter of credit usage and swap position at 2026-09-30, and current ratings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is for slower reported growth and steady cash conversion. Management cut its full-year sales growth outlook to about 14% from 15% to 17%, kept the adjusted EBITDA margin at about 24% and adjusted free cash flow conversion at about 90% to 110%, and narrowed non-operating expense to USD 75 million to USD 80 million. The outlook implies fourth-quarter group sales 7.07% above a year earlier, which becomes a fall of about 3.09% once the USD 50.0 million of Antares Vision sales is added to the base, so organic and currency change is expected to be negative in the quarter. Long-term customer wins that management says enhance visibility, synergy delivery and the order book are tailwinds; lower hardware and vending volumes, trade uncertainty and interest expense that rose 33.11% over nine months are headwinds.

fields.value: Over three to five years the main items are the conversion of the Antares Vision Class B shares by a multiplier of zero to three on 2028 revenue and EBIT, which could raise minority claims if targets are met, and the revolver and Term Loan A falling due in 2030 and the Term Loan B in 2032, where refinancing will depend on leverage at that time and on ratings.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D19; calculation D20; calculation D38

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with a banknote award that slips out of the year while payments and inspection volumes stay weak. Security and authentication carries the profit gain, so a delay cuts currency volumes first; its nine-month operating profit rose USD 40.4 million, and if that gain were lost with net debt unchanged, last-twelve-months reported EBITDA would be USD 333.0 million, net debt over reported EBITDA would rise to 3.40x and EBITDA cover of cash interest would fall to 5.02x. Liquidity would hold, with USD 821.2 million available and no bank maturity before 2030-12-15, and interest would stay covered, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress. The year-end deleveraging target would be missed while the permitted maximum steps down to 4.75x at 2026-12-31, and floating-rate debt at 60.94% would add cost if rates rose; management levers are capital expenditure timing, the dividend of USD 0.18 per share a quarter, cost actions and integration savings, and whether these are enough against a covenant whose definition is not supplied is not established.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation D26; calculation D8; calculation D39; calculation D6; calculation D40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Crane NXT presents an adequate business profile supported by specialised security and authentication technology, an order book covering about two years and strong cash generation, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-led leverage of 3.03x reported EBITDA, a shrinking payments and inspection segment and award concentration. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is 63.07% of reported EBITDA, although it depends on lumpy awards. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on deleveraging towards the company's reported 2.5x on a verified basis, the agencies' view after the Antares Vision financing and covenant headroom through the step-downs. The primary downside path is a delayed banknote award that holds leverage above 3.03x as the covenant maximum falls. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and compliance certificates, Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31, the fourth-quarter 2025 release and current ratings.
